title: Staged deployment playbook & uptime burn chart
summary: A compact operational playbook for phased releases with an integrated uptime burn chart to track SLO consumption across rollout phases and trigger containment actions.
body:
Purpose:
Provide a single-sheet operational checklist for staged deployments that couples traffic ramping rules with a live 'uptime burn' concept: visualize how much of our error-budget/SLO headroom is used at each stage and require guardrails before continuing. Audience: product-ops leads, on-call SREs, release engineers, and engineering managers.

Quick primer on the uptime burn concept:
- Uptime burn = proportion of SLO budget consumed over the rollout window. If SLO remaining drops below thresholds (see triggers) we hold or rollback.
- Track SLO (e.g., 99.9% availability) in rolling 1h and 24h windows. Show delta from baseline during each ramp step.

Rollout cadence (recommended default):
- Canary (1% traffic): 0–2 hours. Automated smoke tests + manual checks. If green, advance.
- Ramp 1 (10%): 2–8 hours. Observe for anomalies at P95 and error rate.
- Ramp 2 (50%): 8–24 hours. Run longitudinal regressions (quality checks).
- Full (100%): Post 24h signoff. Monitor 72h stability.

Gating thresholds (hard stops):
- Immediate rollback if: error rate > 2% OR total customer facing errors spike > 5x baseline in 15min.
- Hold and investigate if: P95 latency increases by >50% vs baseline OR SLO remaining < 92% (1h window).
- Soft alert and watch if: cost per 1k requests increases by >20% or non-critical errors rise.

Preflight checklist (must be green before Canary):
- Release artifacts built and tagged, image checksum verified.
- Canary config and routing policy reviewed (owner: Release Eng).
- Smoke test suite run against canary instances (owner: QA).
- Observability dashboards (latency, errors, top endpoints) pinned to release board.
- Run 'dark traffic' replay for high-risk paths where possible.

Smoke tests (automated):
- Login/auth flows, feature-flag toggles, top 20 user journeys, simple end-to-end generation path for top model.
- Test must include latency assertions and correctness asserts (sample checks).

Observability queries (examples to paste into dashboards):
- Error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",status!~"2.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api"}[1m]))
- P95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- SLO remaining (1h window): 100 * (1 - (errors_1h / total_requests_1h) / (1 - target_error_rate))

Uptime burn chart (how to read and use):
- X axis: rollout phase (Canary -> Ramp1 -> Ramp2 -> Full).
- Y axis left: SLO remaining (%) plotted as dots/line.
- Y axis right: traffic % (stacked bars).
- Annotate with events (smoke-test-pass, manual signoff, rollback).
- Interpretation: steep drops in SLO remaining during low traffic imply high risk — stop and investigate.

Runbook and escalation matrix:
- If hold condition: page SRE on-call (pager: #oncall-sre), create a triage channel (#deploy-triage-<release-id>), freeze further ramps.
- If immediate rollback: follow rollback playbook (owner: Release Eng). Prioritize restoring baseline capacity and routing.
- If noisy signals but below hard stop: engage feature owner and dev author for root-cause hypotheses.

Communication plan (during rollout):
- Canary start: Slack announcement in #release-notifs with artifacts, owners, and monitoring links.
- Hold/rollback: immediate update with reason, metrics snapshot, and next steps.
- Full complete: post in product channels with short summary and link to postmortem prep doc.

Signoff criteria for each ramp (check all):
- No hard stop triggers in 30–60 minute observation window (depending on phase).
- Smoke tests stable (pass count unchanged).
- SLO remaining > 95% for Canary and > 97% for Ramp phases (configurable by risk).
- No unresolved high-severity alerts.

Post-deploy followups:
- 24h recap: quick metrics snapshot (P95, error rate, SLO remaining, cost delta). Owner: Product Ops.
- 72h stability review: decision to revert any config or optimizations made during rollout. Owner: SRE + Product.
- Postmortem if rollback occurred or if any hard-stop threshold was met.

Contingency playbooks (examples):
- Partial traffic split: route traffic away from failing region to healthy region if geo-affected.
- Model fallback: automatically route to previous model variant when quality regressions detected.
- Read-only mode: if downstream write systems are impacted, flip feature flag to read-only for affected endpoints.

One-page checklist (quick scan on release day):
- [ ] Artifact build + checksum verified
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned
- [ ] Canary routing + feature flags configured
- [ ] Smoke tests pass (automated)
- [ ] Manual canary validation complete
- [ ] Ramp thresholds validated
- [ ] Communications plan posted
- [ ] On-call notified and escalation channel open

Notes and open questions (work-in-progress):
- Evaluate whether SLO remaining thresholds should be adaptive based on time-of-day traffic patterns.
- Add a small synthetic traffic generator during Canary for low-traffic windows.
- Consider adding a preflight cost-estimate step for quantization or model-size changes.

Appendix: sample KPIs to log per-phase (recommended columns in the tracking sheet):
- phase_name, start_ts, end_ts, traffic_pct, requests_total, errors_total, error_rate_pct, p95_latency_ms, slo_remaining_pct, smoke_pass (Y/N), actions_taken, owner, notes

End of sheet. Keep this file as the canonical compressed playbook for small-to-medium feature rollouts. If this is used frequently, we will extract a templated Google Sheet with live Prometheus links and a burn chart widget.
notes: Drafted to fill a gap: couples traffic ramp steps directly to SLO burn thresholds and provides concise runbook actions. Intentionally concise to fit on a single sheet for shift leads.
